Orbits and look angles

Azimuth quadrants

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how signed east and north components determine the antenna bearing.

Project the line of sight onto local east and north directions. With station latitude Lₑ, subpoint latitude Lₛ, and longitude difference Δλ, proportional components are E = cos Lₛ sin Δλ and N = sin Lₛ cos Lₑ − cos Lₛ sin Lₑ cos Δλ.

The cartographic bearing is Az = atan2(E, N), wrapped into 0°–360°. North is 0° and east is 90°. Keeping both signs resolves all four quadrants without a separate inverse-sine ambiguity.

Azimuth describes a horizontal direction; visibility requires an elevation calculation as well. A purely radial line of sight has E = N = 0, making its azimuth undefined.

Example

Equal positive east and north components give 45°. Equal negative components give 225°, even though their unsigned component ratio is the same.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. A line of sight has proportional horizontal components E = −2 and N = 2. Find its azimuth and quadrant.

    The satellite lies west of north. Evaluate atan2(E, N), then wrap a negative angle.

    atan2(−2, 2) = −45°, which wraps to 315°. The horizontal direction is northwest.
